# Control the Context, Control the Answer {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

The cleanest proof of the two layers

## The Problem with a Blank Prompt {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="intro" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.15em;"}
**Earlier today:** the brain has amnesia — it only knows what's on the desk.
:::

. . .

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.15em; margin-top: 1em;"}
So put the **right sources** on the desk — and make it answer from **those only.**
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-note}
## The goal
Without **grounding** in real sources, even the smartest brain will **guess.**
:::

# The "Context First" Rule {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #FF7A5C)"}

Stop asking. Start interrogating.

## Wrong Way vs. Right Way {auto-animate=true}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #FF7A5C;"}
**Wrong**

"Summarize the literature on active learning."

→ Generic, maybe fabricated citations.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #00C9A7;"}
**Right**

Upload 5 papers → "Based **only** on these, summarize…"

→ Specific, citable, defensible.
:::
:::
::::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
No upload = no trust. Context comes **before** content.
:::

## The Golden Rule {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.3em;"}
**If it doesn't have a citation, it didn't happen.**
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.6em;"}
For research, teaching materials, and committee work — demand the page reference.
:::

# Meet NotebookLM {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #9B8EC0)"}

A research assistant grounded in *your* documents

## What It's Best At {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="nlm" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #9B8EC0;"}
**Deep reading of big documents** (50+ pages). It builds a guide **solely from your
uploaded sources** — no internet guessing — and every answer links back to the source.
:::

. . .

::: {.incremental}
- Upload papers, a thesis, a policy, lecture readings
- Ask questions; get answers **with citations** to the exact passage
- Generate an **Audio Overview** to listen on your commute
:::

## NotebookLM Now Builds Slides {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="slides" style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.1em;"}
Turn your sources into a **presentation** — grounded in the same documents.
:::

. . .

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #00C9A7;"}
**Detailed Deck**

Text-rich, stands on its own. Good for a reading or handout.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #9B8EC0;"}
**Presenter Slides**

Clean and visual — supports you while you talk.
:::
:::
::::

## Steering & Editing the Deck {auto-animate=true}

::: {.incremental}
- **Before generating:** name your audience, emphasize themes, or structure it around
  specific questions
- **Export** straight to **`.pptx`** — editable PowerPoint
- **Revise** any slide: a pencil icon → type how to change the wording, emphasis, or visual
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-note}
## One requirement
You need **at least one source uploaded** before it can build a deck — grounding first,
always.
:::

# Right Tool, Right Job {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

Cowork, NotebookLM, Deep Research

## Choosing the Tool {auto-animate=true}

| Need | Tool | Why |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Your day-to-day, your files | **Cowork** | One assistant, your folder + rules |
| Read a 100-page PDF, build a deck | **NotebookLM** | Grounded in your docs only |
| Live web with citations | **Deep Research** | Real-time, footnoted |

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; color: #666; font-size: 0.9em; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
*Deep Research = Perplexity / ChatGPT / Gemini. NotebookLM only reads your docs — that's the point.*

:::

# Build: 10-Hour Read in 10 Minutes {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #FF7A5C)"}

Source → grounded summary → deck

## Your Mission {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="mission" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px;"}
Take a **real (safe) paper or policy PDF**. Produce a **1-page grounded summary** and a
**presenter deck** — in 10 minutes.
:::

. . .

::: {.incremental}
1. **Upload** the source to NotebookLM
2. **Interrogate:** *"Based only on this, give 5 key findings with page references. If it's
   not in the source, say 'Not found.'"*
3. **Verify** the citations — click through to the passage
4. **Generate** a Presenter deck → export `.pptx` → revise one slide
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip}
## Log it
10 minutes vs. the hours it used to take. That's the number for the **Wrap-up**.
:::

# Micro-Check {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #9B8EC0)"}

Pick the right move

:::

## Key Takeaways {.sdaia-dark background-color="#1C355E"}

::: {.incremental}
1. **Context before content** — never start from a blank prompt
2. **Grounding builds trust** — upload sources, constrain to "only these"
3. **No citation = didn't happen** — demand page references
4. **NotebookLM** — deep reading **and** decks (Detailed vs. Presenter, `.pptx`)
5. **Right tool, right job** — Cowork / NotebookLM / Deep Research
:::
